name: The Alcubierre warp-drive metric is neither static nor spherically symmetric

source.located: arXiv:gr-qc/0009013v1 (posted 5 Sep 2000) = M. Alcubierre, 'The warp drive: hyper-fast travel within general relativity', Class. Quantum Grav. 11 (1994) L73-L77. All ten pages returned.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries(paper='gr-qc/0009013', 10 queries in one call)

published_statement: Eq (1)-(5): 3+1 form with lapse alpha = 1, shift beta^x = -v_s(t) f(r_s(t)), beta^y = beta^z = 0, gamma_ij = delta_ij, v_s(t) = dx_s/dt, r_s = [(x - x_s(t))^2 + y^2 + z^2]^{1/2}. Eq (6): f(r_s) = [tanh(sigma(r_s+R)) - tanh(sigma(r_s-R))]/(2 tanh(sigma R)), R > 0, sigma > 0 arbitrary; Eq (7): f -> top hat as sigma -> infinity. Eq (8): ds^2 = -dt^2 + (dx - v_s f(r_s) dt)^2 + dy^2 + dz^2. 'The 3-geometry of the hypersurfaces is always flat'; alpha = 1 so 'the Eulerian observers are in free fall'; 'Spacetime, however, is not flat due to the presence of a non-uniform shift'; 'at any time t spacetime will be essentially flat everywhere except within a region with a radius of order R, centered at the point (x_s(t),0,0)'. Eq (12): theta = v_s (x_s/r_s) df/dr_s [sic; x - x_s meant], Figure 1 plotted against x and rho = (y^2+z^2)^{1/2}. Eq (13): dtau = dt on the ship's path, a geodesic. Eq (19): T^{mu nu} n_mu n_nu = alpha^2 T^{00} = G^{00}/8pi = -(1/8pi) v_s^2 rho^2/(4 r_s^2) (df/dr_s)^2, 'everywhere negative', so 'it violates all three energy conditions (weak, dominant and strong)'; 'exotic matter will be needed'. The paper never uses the words 'static' or 'spherically symmetric', and never writes T^{0i}: the three properties the tree uses (not static, not spherically symmetric, T^{0i} != 0) are consequences of Eq (8), derived here, not sentences of the source.
published_hypotheses: General relativity, G = c = 1, no matter model: T_mu_nu is read off from G_mu_nu of the prescribed metric (Eq 19)
3+1 form with lapse alpha = 1 and flat slices gamma_ij = delta_ij (Eqs 2, 5)
Shift along the direction of motion only, beta^x = -v_s(t) f(r_s), with x_s(t) an ARBITRARY function of time (Eq 3-4)
Shape function f of Eq (6), R > 0 and sigma > 0 arbitrary; the top-hat limit Eq (7)
The spaceship is a test particle on x = x_s(t) (Eq 13: dtau = dt, a geodesic)
Energy density is measured by the Eulerian observers n^mu = (1, -beta^i) (Eq 18)
Global hyperbolicity claimed from positive-definiteness of gamma_ij alone (p.3-4) -- a claim the tree does not use, and one BBV 2602.16495 Error 1 shows is false in general
hypothesis_drift: certify.py:181-182 'the Alcubierre drive is neither [static nor spherically symmetric]': NOT a sentence of the source; DERIVED here and it holds. For constant v_s the Killing field xi = d_t + v_s d_x has twist (xi^dxi)_{txy} = -v_s f_y [1 + v_s^2 (1-f)^2] (symbolic, residual 0), non-zero wherever d_y f != 0 (0.549 at (0.9,0.3), v_s = 0.5); adding any multiple of the axial Killing field y d_z - z d_y leaves that component unchanged (symbolic, 0), and the invariants R and Ric^2 have independent gradients in the (x', rho) plane (normalised cross product 0.047), so the surface on which every invariant is constant is the 2-surface spanned by xi (timelike there: xi.xi = -0.977) and the rotation -- it cannot be an SO(3) orbit. No drift; the owner's status 'none (named)' understates it: it is now computed.

phase1.py:255 'The shift vector gives T^{0i} != 0' and phase1.py:256 (hard-coded True): NOT stated in the source (the paper gives only T^{00}). Computed here: T^{0y} = v_xy/(16 pi), T^{0z} = v_xz/(16 pi), T^{0x} = -(v_yy+v_zz)/(16 pi) - v(v_y^2+v_z^2)/(32 pi) with v = v_s f, non-zero in the wall off-axis (T^{0x} = 0.0877, T^{0y} = -0.0524 at (0.9,0.3)); restated in closed form by Lobo & Visser gr-qc/0406083 Eqs (A2)-(A4), (A12)-(A14). The tree's assertion is true but was never computed in the tree; it is now.

phase1.py:92-94 'it fails automatically for anything with a shift vector': ADDED generalisation wider than what holds. A uniform shift (f == 1 everywhere) gives G == 0 exactly (symbolic, True) -- flat space in sheared coordinates; Natario gr-qc/0110086 Corollary 1.6 restates it (flat wherever X is a Euclidean Killing field). The source says 'non-uniform shift' (p.5). The Alcubierre-specific verdict (phase1.py:62-64, :408-409) is unaffected because its shift is non-uniform by construction.

typefour.py:138 (imported by anec.py:41-42, :94-117): 'The configuration is static in these coordinates, so d_t g = 0' -- DROPS the source's x_s(t). In the published coordinates x_s = v_s t and d_t g = -v_s d_x g != 0 in the wall; the frozen metric (shift v_s f(x,y,z), time-independent) is a DIFFERENT spacetime: Ricci scalar 8.29 (published) vs -1.40 (frozen) at (0.9,0.3); T_yy -0.159 vs +0.033, and Lobo-Visser (A5) closed form -0.159191 agrees with the published, not the frozen. Symbolically, published - frozen = 0 for T_tt, T_tx, T_xx; = v_s^2 f_xx/(8 pi) for T_yy and T_zz; = -v_s^2 f_xy/(16 pi) for T_xy -- exactly -(v_s/8pi)(d_x K_ij - delta_ij d_x K) (residual 0). CONSEQUENCE FOR anec.py: none. T_kk for any k in the t-x plane is identical (anec.T_kk = -0.188762 vs sympy published -0.188762), and all five ANEC integrals agree to 4e-8 (y = 0.0: -0.080665 / -0.080665; y = 0.8: -0.344100 / -0.344100). typefour's two validations (vacuum floor, BBV Eq 3.48 for T^00) cannot see the discrepancy because rho_E and J_i come from the constraint equations, which see only derivatives of the shift. Recorded, not repaired.

anec.py:102 rays k = (1, v+1, 0, 0) along y = const: off-axis these are null but NOT geodesics -- a^y = d_y v (symbolic); on the axis a is parallel to k with kappa = d_x v (non-affine in t). ANEC is defined on complete null geodesics, so anec.py's off-axis integrals are along non-geodesic null curves, and its int T_kk dx at fixed t = 0 is not an affine integral along any geodesic of the moving spacetime. On the one geodesic in its sample (axis, forward) the affine integral on the published metric is -0.0772 (dt-weighted -0.109; anec's dx-weighted -0.0807): sign survives. The BACKWARD axis geodesic (k^x = v-1), which anec.py does not sample, gives +0.0828 (affine): 'NEGATIVE ON EVERY RAY' (anec.py:47) is true of the forward rays only. ANEC violation needs one geodesic, so the conclusion stands; the sample description does not. This is a hypothesis the importer adds, not one the source carries.

anec.py:90 / typefour.py:99-101 v_s = 0.5, sigma = 8, R = 1 (twist.py v_s = 0.9) against the source's Figure-1 values sigma = 8, R = v_s = 1: a parameter choice inside the source's 'arbitrary' v_s(t), sigma, R -- not a drift.

composite.py:83-88 'the rays that turn are the rays that pass through positive T_kk': not in the source, not measured here; the source says nothing about focusing. Recorded as the tree's own claim, outside this result.

Eq (12) as printed, theta = v_s (x_s/r_s) df/dr_s: with x_s = v_s t literally the residual against -Tr K is v_s (x - 2 v_s t) f'/r_s != 0; with x_s read as (x - x_s) the residual is 0. Natario (p.4) and Alcubierre-Lobo 2103.05610 Eq (4) both write (x - x_s)/r_s. A notational misprint, a discrepancy and not a refutation; the tree does not use Eq (12).

rederivation.outcome: exit 0; output in gr-qc_0009013.out.txt / .out.json beside it. (1) typefour.shape == Eq (6) to 0.0 at 7 radii; Eq (7) limit reproduced. (2) Eq (19) reproduced as a symbolic identity in a generic shift v(t,x,y,z): G^00/8pi = -(v_y^2+v_z^2)/(32 pi), and in f: residual 0 against -(1/32pi) v_s^2 rho^2/r_s^2 f'^2; numeric -0.0028662 at (0.9,0.3) = typefour.eulerian_density = BBV Eq (3.48). (3) T^{0i} closed forms (above), non-zero in the wall; uniform shift gives G == 0. (4) xi = d_t + v_s d_x is Killing (Lie_xi g = 0), its twist -v_s f_y[1+v_s^2(1-f)^2] (residual 0), unchanged by any multiple of the axial Killing field: NOT STATIC. (5) Independent invariant gradients at (0.9,0.3), xi timelike there: NOT SPHERICALLY SYMMETRIC. (6) Eq (12) = -Tr K with x_s read as x - x_s; theta = +2.0 behind, -2.0 ahead at v_s = 1 (expansion behind). (7) typefour's frozen-x_s metric differs from the published one in R, T_yy, T_zz, T_xy only, by exactly -(v_s/8pi)(d_x K_ij - delta_ij d_x K); T_tt, T_tx, T_xx identical, so every anec.py number is reproduced (ANEC integrals to 4e-8; T_kk to 1e-6, the pipeline's own noise); Lobo-Visser (A5) and (A10) closed forms match the published metric to 1e-7. typefour's Hawking-Ellis type re-measured on the published metric: |Im|/||T|| = 0.57, 0.33, 0.28, 0.31, 0.43, 0.11, 0.049 at its seven wall points (frozen: 0.14, 0.22, 0.64, 0.31, 0.26, 0.54, 0.69) -- numbers change at six of seven points, all remain above its 1e-3 threshold: Type IV survives. Axis null geodesic, affinely parametrised, on the published metric: forward -0.0772, backward +0.0828.

later_literature.what: Appendix A gives the full orthonormal Einstein tensor for Alcubierre's metric with x_s(t): G_tx, G_ty, G_tz != 0 (A2-A4, A12-A14) -- the momentum density the tree asserts; (A5) and (A10) match this audit's published-metric stresses to 1e-7 and disagree with typefour's frozen T_yy. Also: NEC violated for all v including v << 1, the 'reaction-less drive' reading, and z' = z - vt makes the metric 'look static' (their word; it is stationary).

Generalises to any bounded shift X: expansion is 'a marginal consequence' of Alcubierre's choice (zero-expansion drive exists); Cor. 1.6 flat wherever X is a Euclidean Killing field (the uniform-shift point); Thm 1.7 non-flat warp drives violate WEC or SEC; stationary only if |v_s| < 1; writes theta = v_s f'(r_s)(x - x_s)/r_s and rho = -(1/32pi) v_s^2 f'^2 (y^2+z^2)/r_s^2.

Restates Eq (12) with (z - z_0)/r (their Eq 4), Eq (19) as their Eq (8), Pfenning-Ford's Delta <= 10^2 v_b L_Planck and E <= -3e20 M_galaxy v_b, the horizon/control problem (Hiscock's 2D reduction in manifestly static form for v_b < 1, Eq 36: the non-staticity of the 4D metric lives in the transverse gradient d_y f, off the axis), Lobo-Visser's v^2 R^2 sigma <= M_ship.

Comoving representation N^i = -V_s(t)[f(r_s)-1] (3.44); E = -Omega^2/(8 pi G) (3.48) -- the identity typefour validates against; Theorem III.15 (vorticity-free Alcubierre is Minkowski); Error 1: Alcubierre's argument that positive-definite gamma_ij implies global hyperbolicity is false in general -- narrows a claim of the 1994 paper the tree does not use; Errors 13, 31, 33 contest Fuchs et al. 2405.02709.
Quantum-inequality bound on the wall thickness and total energy -- a feasibility limit on the configuration, not a change to the metric's properties; the tree holds it (certify.py:22-30).

later_literature.what: Generic (Natario-class) warp drives violate the NEC; refutes positive-energy claims.
Finite-difference T_mu_nu from the metric, energy conditions over sampled observers: Alcubierre violates all four (their Table 1; certify.py:50-56 restates).
Claims a constant-velocity subluminal warp solution satisfying the energy conditions; BBV 2602.16495 Errors 13, 31, 33 dispute it.
Later formal treatments of energy conditions over all causal directions and of the shift's symmetry; returned by discover_papers, not read.
2D axial reduction admits a static form ds^2 = -A dtau^2 + dr^2/A with A = 1 - v_b^2(1-f)^2 for v_b < 1, and a horizon at f = 1 - 1/v_b for v_b > 1.

lacked_data: The 1994 result uses no empirical datum: G = c = 1 and three free parameters, so there is nothing M's hypothesis could have supplied that would move it, and the re-derivation reproduces Eq (19), the twist, and T^{0i} with no inputs at all -- evidence against the hypothesis for this result. What Alcubierre lacked was later THEORY, and it moved his framing, not his metric: Natario 2001 showed the expansion/contraction 'mechanism' is inessential; Ford-Roman/Pfenning-Ford 1995-97 bounded the wall and the energy; Hiscock, Everett, Krasnikov 1996-98 found the horizon and the control problem for v_s > 1; Lobo-Visser 2004 read the shift's momentum density as a reaction-less drive; BBV 2026 (Error 1) showed his global-hyperbolicity argument does not hold in general. None of those touches the three properties the tree uses. The only place the tree's own use lacked something is not data either: typefour.py:138 froze x_s(t) and its two validations could not detect it, because rho_E and J_i are constraint quantities blind to the constant shift -- found here by computing the difference, which is closed-form.
grade_evidence: The statement as the tree uses it is three properties of Eq (8), and each is reproduced: (i) not static -- the Killing field's twist -v_s f_y[1+v_s^2(1-f)^2] is non-zero off-axis (symbolic residual 0, 0.549 numeric), and no combination with the axial Killing field removes it; (ii) not spherically symmetric -- independent invariant gradients with a timelike xi in the common level set exclude an SO(3) orbit; (iii) T^{0i} != 0 -- closed forms derived, numeric 0.0877 / -0.0524 at (0.9,0.3), restated by Lobo-Visser (A2)-(A4). The tree's metric and shape function match Eqs (8) and (6) to 0.0. Eq (19) is reproduced symbolically. No datum enters. The drifts found are all in the tree's use and none moves a conclusion drawn from THIS result: phase1.py:92-94's 'any shift vector' is wider than true (uniform shift is flat) but unused for Alcubierre; typefour.py:138's frozen x_s is a different spacetime, yet the t-row and T_xx are identical so every anec.py number is reproduced, and typefour's Type-IV classification survives re-measurement on the published metric (min ratio 0.049 against 1e-3); anec.py's off-axis rays are not geodesics and its backward axis geodesic is ANEC-positive (+0.083), but the forward axis geodesic is negative (-0.077) so ANEC violation stands. A misprint in Eq (12) is a discrepancy, not a refutation.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if any importer of typefour used T_yy, T_zz or T_xy as a statement about Alcubierre's metric without the correction v_s^2 f_xx/(8 pi), -v_s^2 f_xy/(16 pi) -- the Type-IV classification is the one such importer found, and it survives (re-measured here); or if the tree's D4 test were read in a frame other than the Eulerian one (T^{0i} is frame-dependent; a frame with T^{0i} = 0 everywhere would be a rest frame, which typefour's Type IV says does not exist at the wall points, and that consistency has not been made a theorem). WRONG only by a hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing field outside span{d_t + v_s d_x, y d_z - z d_y} -- excluded at the tested points by the invariant-gradient argument, which is pointwise, not global. The ANEC conclusion in anec.py would fall if the forward axis geodesic's affine integral changed sign under a finer integration (h = 2e-3 used, -0.0772 against a dt-weighted -0.109; not a marginal number).
